It is further submitted that respondent and her husband lived with the father-in-law and mother-in-law together only for a brief period of 2.5 years from the date of their marriage and for any alleged incident of domestic violence, there should be a subsisting domestic relationship and there was a domestic relationship with the father-in-law and mother-in-law for a brief period of only 2.5 years i.e. from 2008 to 2010.
Thereafter, they never lived together.

The marriage between respondent and Satish Garg was solemnized in 2008 while the complaint was filed in 2021 i.e. after a period of almost 13 years from the date of her marriage alleging acts of domestic violence since her marriage.
Hence, there is an unexplained gross delay in filing a complaint alleging domestic violence.
The allegations in the DIR dated 28.08.2021 against the appellants are unsubstantiated and are not supported by any cogent evidence and documents.

Hence, the DIR is devoid of corroborative evidence to substantiate the allegations and the complaint under the DV Act against the appellants is a counterblast to Divorce proceedings between the respondent and her husband Satish Garg and complaint has been falsely filed to use as a pressure tactics to KUMAR by KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT Date: 2024.11.12 17:41:00 +0530

Trial Court and the husband was summoned on 26.07.2021 and the summoning of other respondents was kept in abeyance after the consideration of DIR in which there are allegations against the husband and other respondents including appellants and Ld.

Trial was directed to consider the issue of summoning the other respondents after considering the DIR filed in 2021 and Lalita Garg filed a revision petition before the Sessions Court against the order of Ld. Trial Court directing her to pay EMI of the loan taken of the shared house-hold from Aditya Birla Financing Institution, which was jointly owned by her and her son Satish Garg, who is husband of complainant and the said revision was dismissed vide order dated 25.03.2023 and cost of Rs. 50,000/- was imposed on them and Lalita Garg has filed one petition before Ghaziabad Court against the complainant and her family members under DV Act on false averments to harass and humiliate her and her family members.
9. I have heard the rival contentions and perused the record.

As regards the contention of appellants in the application u/s 5 of the Limitation Act that due to the lack of legal knowledge and the fact that previous counsel did not tell them about the fact that impugned order was an appealable order, due to which they could not challenge the said order, it is settled law that ignorance of law is no excuse.

The second application for condonation of delay is also defective, as the averments are copy pasted from the application in another appeal despite it being filed second time as previous application was also defective, but the Court has taken the oral arguments on behalf of the appellant.

However, considering the fact that appellants were not aware of legal nuances and in the judgment of Collector (Supra),
Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that refusing to condone the delay can result in meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold and 'every day's delay must be explained' does not mean that a pedantic approach should be adopted and when substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other,
the former deserves to be preferred and ordinarily a litigant does not stand to benefit by filing late appeals.

In Rafiq (Supra), it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that contesting parties should not suffer due to lapses on part of their counsel and in N Balakrishnan (Supra), it was held that sufficient cause should be construed liberally and delay of 883 days was condoned.

The marriage between the complainant and her husband Satish Garg was solemnized on 22.04.2008 at Ghaziabad, UP and complainant came to her matrimonial home at R4-B, Dishad Garden, Delhi.

As per Section 2(f) of DV Act: "Domestic relationship"
means a relationship between two persons who live or have, any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
12.
The domestic violence is defined in Section 3 of the DV Act and includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse.

13. As per Section 2(f), if at any point of time, two persons have lived together in shared house-hold and related through relationship in marriage or are family members living together as a joint family are set to be in domestic relationship and shared house-hold is defined in Section 2(s) that "Shared household", means a household where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such a household whether owned or tenanted either Digitally signed by KUMAR KUMAR

Date:
RAJAT RAJAT 2024.11.12 17:41:32 +0530 jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in respect of which either the aggrieved person or the respondent or both jointly or singly have any right, title,
interest or equity and includes such a household which may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the share household.
14. As per averment in the appeal, there was no domestic relationship between complainant and appellants.
Nand of the complainant namely Kavita Goyal was married in 2004 and has never lived in her parental home after marriage.
15. As per the Domestic Incident Report, the parents of the complainant had spent huge amount of money in the marriage as per their capacity including gold jewellery, house-hold articles, cash etc.

As regards the limitation argued by the Ld. Counsel for the appellants that the DV petition was filed with delay and summoning was done with great delay, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kamatchi Vs. Laxmi Narayanan AIR 2022 SC 2932 that the provisions of DV Act contemplate filing of an application u/s 12 to initiate the proceedings before the concerned Magistrate.

entities.text: Kamatchi Vs. Laxmi Narayanan AIR 2022 SC 2932
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing both sides and after taking into account, the material on record, the Magistrate may pass an appropriate order u/s 12 of the DV Act.
It is only the breach of such order which constitutes an offence as is clear from Section 31 of the Act.
Thus, if there be any offence committed in terms of the provisions of the Act, the limitation prescribed u/s 468 of Cr.P.C. will apply from the date of commission of offence.

By the time an application is preferred u/s 12 DV Act, there is no offence committed in terms of the provisions of the Act and as such there would never be a starting point for limitation from the date of application u/s 12 DV Act and it will arise only when there is breach of any order passed u/s 12 of the Act.

The judgments cited by Ld. Counsel for the appellants are not applicable to the facts of the present case qua appellant no. 1 & 2.

The order of the Ld. Trial Court dated 20.02.2023 is not sustainable qua appellant no. 3 Kavita Goyal and holds good qua appellants Hari Kishan Garg and Jyoti as they had lived with complainant in his joint family and shared household after her marriage and there are specific allegations against them.

The judgments cited by Ld. Counsel for the appellants are not applicable to the facts of the present case as in those judgments of Sushil Kumar Sharma (Supra) and Savitri Devi (Supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court had dealt with the provisions of Section 498A/406 IPC and the provisions of DV Act are entirely different and they are brought to safeguard the women from being the victims of domestic violence and to prevent domestic violence in the society.
CONCLUSION 20.

Considering the DIR as well as the complaint u/s 12 of the DV Act, wherein specific allegations have been made KUMAR by KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT 17:42:02 Date: 2024.11.12 +0530 against the appellant no. 1 and 2 Hari Kishan Garg and Jyoti by the respondent/complainant, the order of Ld.
Trial Court does not appear to be without any application of mind and it was passed after considering the said material and the specific allegations against the appellants and they were summoned accordingly and as such the said order dated 20.02.2023 does not suffer from any material illegality and as such does not need any interference from this Court.
21.
As regards appellant no. 3 Kavita Goyal, the said order dated 20.02.2023 is set aside and she is discharged from the proceedings of DV Act before the Ld. Trial Court.
22. Hence, the appeal is partly allowed and is accordingly disposed of.
23. Nothing mentioned herein shall tantamount to any expression on the merits of the case.
Copy of judgment be sent to Ld. Trial Court with TCR and be uploaded on the website.
The appeal file be consigned to Record Room after necessary compliance.

Considering the DIR as well as the complaint u/s 12 of the DV Act, wherein specific allegations have been made KUMAR by KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT 17:42:02 Date: 2024.11.12 +0530 against the appellant no. 1 and 2 Hari Kishan Garg and Jyoti by the respondent/complainant, the order of Ld.
Trial Court does not appear to be without any application of mind and it was passed after considering the said material and the specific allegations against the appellants and they were summoned accordingly and as such the said order dated 20.02.2023 does not suffer from any material illegality and as such does not need any interference from this Court.
21.
As regards appellant no. 3 Kavita Goyal, the said order dated 20.02.2023 is set aside and she is discharged from the proceedings of DV Act before the Ld. Trial Court.
22. Hence, the appeal is partly allowed and is accordingly disposed of.
23. Nothing mentioned herein shall tantamount to any expression on the merits of the case.
Copy of judgment be sent to Ld. Trial Court with TCR and be uploaded on the website.
The appeal file be consigned to Record Room after necessary compliance.
